questions.question_html: In Linear Programming Problem (LPP), the objective function $Z=ax+by$ has the same maximum value at two corner points. The number of points at which $Z_{max}$ occurs is
questions.explanation_text: If the objective function $Z=ax+by$ has the same maximum value at two corner points of the feasible region, then $Z$ will have the same value at every point on the line segment joining those two corner points. This happens because $Z=ax+by$ is a linear function. So, if it is maximum at two endpoints of an edge of the feasible region, then it remains maximum at all points on that edge. Hence, $Z_{max}$ occurs at infinitely many points. So, the correct option is: $\text{Option D: Infinity}$
questions.explanation_html:
If the objective function $Z=ax+by$ has the same maximum value at two corner points of the feasible region, then $Z$ will have the same value at every point on the line segment joining those two corner points.

This happens because $Z=ax+by$ is a linear function. So, if it is maximum at two endpoints of an edge of the feasible region, then it remains maximum at all points on that edge.

Hence, $Z_{max}$ occurs at infinitely many points.

So, the correct option is:

$\text{Option D: Infinity}$

Statement (I): In a LPP, the objective function is always linear.

questions.explanation_text: Option A. Both statements are true. Reasoning: By definition, a Linear Programming Problem (LPP) has a linear objective function, for example $maxz=c_{1}x_{1}+c_{2}x_{2}+\cdot s+c_{n}x_{n}.$ The restrictions on the variables take the form of linear inequalities (or equalities), such as $a_{i1}x_{1}+a_{i2}x_{2}+\cdot s+a_{in}x_{n} \le b_{i},$ and these are called constraints.
questions.explanation_html:
Option A. Both statements are true.

Reasoning:

By definition, a Linear Programming Problem (LPP) has a linear objective function, for example

$maxz=c_{1}x_{1}+c_{2}x_{2}+\cdot s+c_{n}x_{n}.$

The restrictions on the variables take the form of linear inequalities (or equalities), such as

$a_{i1}x_{1}+a_{i2}x_{2}+\cdot s+a_{in}x_{n} \le b_{i},$

and these are called constraints.
